en: All your vaunted elders,
As though struck by slaughter,
Go and perish together!
Has the bloodthirsty son of Manas
Recited some spell from scripture
And mounted it as his steed?
His dapple-gray horse was his wings;
Dark-flanked and blue-backed,
That fiery bloodthirsty warrior
Turned back after besieging Kakan,
But the legacy of that entrusted bread—
His Buurul—has been taken from him.
Blood has flooded his breast;
Deprived of Buurul,
His good fortune has deserted him.
Leaning upon Akkelte,
He has been left on foot;
Your shambling bloodthirsty foe
Is fated to die a foul death this year!
Among all the horses God created,
What champion steed remains
To lift and carry that man?
That reckless bloodthirsty warrior
Is fated to die this year.
The reason he must die is this:
The forty calamities have overtaken him;
His Buurul has vanished from his grasp
And all his blessings have scattered.
The forty holy spirits who sustained him
Have withdrawn far from his body.
At the forked, arching mountain pass
He has been left looming there on foot;
Disaster, death, and dread misfortune
Have closed around the hero.
Damn you, Jediger,
Swarm upon him and wage war!
Take your vengeance upon Semetey;
Raid Keng-Kol and seize its herds!
Stately hero Kyyaz,
Take your revenge before departing;
Devastate Talas and seize its herds!
Damn you, Jediger,
Strike tirelessly and take revenge!
This year your turn has come
To gouge out eyes black as currants,
To gorge yourselves upon rich broth
And the fat flesh of royal feasts;
This year your turn has come
To slaughter the gray wolf, the bloodthirsty man’s son!
Why do you not strike down
The bloodthirsty man looming there
And lay him dead upon his back, Jediger?
Why do you not take the vast wealth
Left by his father Manas,
Divide it as spoils, and carry it away?
Do you not see, Jediger,
How boundless his riches are?
Why do you not divide, Jediger,
His countless treasures and myriad goods?
Why do you not behold, Jediger,
Wonders no man has ever seen?
Why do you not launch, Jediger,
A mighty campaign and a great war?
And has not moon-faced Aichürök
Been left proud and unprotected?
Why do you not take her too,
And claim her as your prize, Jediger?
Why do you not finish the bloodthirsty man
And depart, Jediger?
On the hills are piebald herds,
With thoroughbreds and swift coursers mingled;
Why do you not take your share
Of the finest steeds and leave, Jediger?
You stirred and fled, Jediger,
Though your numbers swelled into a nation,
Though you surged like a mighty people!
You have already crossed
Yonder Kara-Buura and Besh-Tash;
You miserable people scattered in fear—
You have fled away!
From his magnanimous father Manas
He inherited and still holds
The red-tailed gun called Bili.
You vast host of Jediger,
Stop snarling and heed my words;
I have spoken precious counsel—understand it!
Seize his herds from the mountain slope;
Ah, slaughter-stricken Jediger,
Sooner or later
You will flee snarling again—
Take your vengeance while you can!
Understand what I have told you;
Ah, Jediger, heed my words!
Here stands Kanchoro, sharp-eyed as a khan,
Who will devise the way to victory.
You fleeing Jediger,
When Külchoro pursued you in fury,
What did you have to say then?
You found the chance to level your spears
And thrust them with proper aim,
Yet by fleeing the warrior, wretched people,
You have broken my back!
You vast host of Jediger,
If you ignore my ceaseless words,
Then sink into the earth, unworthy to be a people!
You have left me helpless.
From along the Seven Valleys
You came surging in great numbers;
You came saying you would overwhelm
The heroic son of Manas.
You vast host of Jediger,
You came with champions and giants aplenty;
Ah, you babbling paupers,
Why did you come, not knowing you would flee?”
He descended upon the hill, roaring;
Kanchoro bellowed
Until the apricot treetops bent:
“You beastly Jediger,
The man you came to fight is Semetey—
What else do you say now?
While you were in the Seven Valleys,
You boasted, ‘I shall seize and slaughter him,’
And began your speech with bravado;
But when you saw Külchoro,
You cried, ‘We have suffered grievously,
We are slaughtered and doomed!’
And cast away your spears.
Rushing about in frantic panic—
Damn you, Jediger—
This is the example you now set!
While you were in the Seven Valleys,
You vowed, ‘I shall catch him and exact blood-price;
I shall fight fiercely for six full months
And grapple with him in carnage!’
You blustered in your haste,
But when you saw Külchoro,
Like a flock struck by a falcon,
You fled wherever your eyes could see!
While you were in the Seven Valleys,
You stood there raging;
But when the time came to face him,
Unable to find your bearings,
You panicked, straining for a plan,
Crying, ‘Now we are slaughtered!’
With what face can you flee?
Understand now what I have said!
Stallion-like hero Kyyaz,
If you are no man, sink into the earth!
Damn you, Jediger,
Understand what I have told you;
My foolish people, heed my words!
Of the many mares brought for provisions,
Catch and slaughter a white mare;
Let us feast together to our fill
On choice meat and rich horse-ribs.
Rather than flee in scattered bands—
Damn you, Jediger—
Let us turn fierce as wolves!
Let us unite our strength in one place—
Damn you, Jediger—
Fire our guns and draw our bows,
And advance to face the enemy!
Let us bring down the accursed bloodthirsty man’s
Banner from Keng-Kol;
Come, wretched people, let us fight
And bury the bloodthirsty man in the earth!
Let Kanchoro and Kyyaz, the two khans,
Set this undertaking right;
Let us destroy this magnanimous khan
Whose forefather was a noble khan,
And take both reins and bridle
Into our own hands!
Let us become khans over his realm,
Men of immeasurably precious lives;
Let us impose our will and rule the people,
And take affairs into our own hands!”
Then Kanchoro,
Seething and enraged,
Was visited, valiant man that he was,
By sudden inspiration from the unseen.
Roaring furiously,
He summoned the vast host of Jediger,
Calling for every last man to come.
They took the many mares kept for provisions
And slaughtered a white mare;
They chose men from among the people,
Saying, “This shall be the fate of anyone who flees,”
And dipped their hands in its blood.
They cut switches and swore by their strength,
Making a solemn covenant;
If any people refused to submit,
They punished them and forced matters straight—
Such was the nature of their cruelty.
Driven to desperation, Kanchoro declared,
“This is what shall befall whoever flees;
And this is how those who do not flee shall stand.”
They chewed white wheaten flour,
Swearing an oath unto death,
And licked the edges of their swords.
Roaring in fury,
He summoned all the people without exception,
And made the vast host of Jediger
Pledge their word in this manner:
“From now on, wretched people,
You have seen what befalls the one who flees;
When I rise in wrath,
You will die before your appointed hour!
Come, all you gray-bearded elders;
Captains of fifty and captains of a thousand,
Let no captain of a hundred remain behind!
Come, all my people, leaving none behind;
Come calmly and keep your wits!
Do not halt, Jediger,
Do not bustle about or raise an uproar,
Do not let the ninety tribes stir strife;
Come surging forward, all my people!
Let your wise and capable men come,
Your resourceful masters of stratagem come;
Let your axe-wielding lions come,
Bull-necked and camel-thighed,
Men who crush all who grapple with them,
Your towering heroes;
Do not falter, Jediger—
Come here now!
Let your thick-armed lions come;
I have something to say, Jediger—
Let the multitude come, leaving none behind.
Let your broad-chested, iron-hearted,
Stately men of Jediger come;
Let your generous heroes come—
Though a thousand stay behind, let your best one come!
Let those who stand beneath the banner come,
Those who, when outright conflict erupts,
At once level their spears!
In the time it takes to turn around,
In the blink of an eye,
Let those whose shouts can split stone,
Who charge in fury and shatter heads,
Come strike where death awaits!
Let your broad-chested lions come,
Who never retreat from their purpose
And never turn back before death;
Let your iron-hearted heroes come,
Who never withdraw from a contest!
When fierce battle-cries arise,
When the tumult no soul can bear erupts,
When the uproar rends the sky,
Let those who wheel their chargers come!
When tremendous turmoil descends,
And their fly-like lives are imperiled,
Let those who never shrink from death,
Who rejoice at the word ‘death’
And never turn back even when dying,
Come—your wolves, your champions against the foe!
Let those who unleash volleys of gunfire come,
Those who take moon-beautiful women as spoils
